summary: Defines the CHILDREN extension for IMAP4, which lets a client learn whether a mailbox has child mailboxes without issuing separate LIST commands for each one. The document title says Message Action Protocol, but the protocol is the Internet Message Access Protocol.

eli5.summary: Mail folders can contain more folders. This extension lets a mail program ask in one go which folders have sub-folders, instead of opening each to check.

subtitle: Two LIST attributes that tell an IMAP client whether a mailbox has child mailboxes, without extra LIST commands.

tldr.problem: Mail clients that show a collapsed mailbox tree need to know which mailboxes have children, but finding out meant issuing a LIST for each mailbox.
tldr.mechanism: A server advertises the CHILDREN capability and may mark each mailbox in a LIST response with \HasChildren or \HasNoChildren.
tldr.outcome: The memo documents behavior that several IMAP vendors had implemented, and it expected a more general LIST extension to carry the idea forward on the standards track.

today: RFC 3348 is an Informational memo, and the unit metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated. It builds on RFC 2060, and the text expected the more general LIST extension work to take over on the standards track.

sections.title: Why the Extension Exists
sections.content:
Many IMAP4 clients (RFC 2060) show a hierarchical view of a user's mailboxes. With many mailboxes it is better to show a collapsed outline, often with a visual clue such as a + beside a mailbox that has child mailboxes. Clicking it expands the list.

To draw that clue, a client needs to know which mailboxes have children. Without this extension it would issue LIST "" * or LIST "" % for each mailbox. The title of the RFC says Message Action Protocol, but the protocol is the Internet Message Access Protocol.

The memo records that several IMAP vendors implemented this proposal. It also expects a more general IMAP LIST Extension to proceed on the standards track, leaving this document as informational only. In that design a client could ask whether the server should compute the information, which helps servers where it is expensive.
sections.eli5: Folder lists show a little plus sign next to folders that have folders inside. This lets the mail program learn which ones need a plus sign without peeking into every folder.

sections.title: The Two Attributes
sections.content:
A server that supports the extension MUST list the keyword CHILDREN in its CAPABILITY response. It MAY then return two new attributes in a LIST response.

  • \HasChildren means the mailbox has child mailboxes.
  • \HasNoChildren means the mailbox has no child mailboxes accessible to the current user.

Servers SHOULD NOT return \HasChildren when children exist but none will be shown to the user, for example because of permissions. They SHOULD use \HasNoChildren then.

Servers often cannot compute this cheaply, so a client MUST treat \HasChildren as a hint. A mailbox may carry it even though no child appears in a later LIST response. A server that cannot tell MAY send neither attribute, so a client cannot infer anything from the absence of one attribute.
sections.eli5: The mail server can put a sticker on each folder saying either it has folders inside or it does not. The sticker is a good guess, not a promise.

sections.title: Rules, Errors and Special Cases
sections.content:
It is an error for a server to return both \HasChildren and \HasNoChildren, or both \HasChildren and \NoInferiors. \HasNoChildren is not the same as the IMAP4 attribute \Noinferiors, which means no children exist now and none can ever be created. If a mailbox has \Noinferiors, \HasNoChildren is redundant and SHOULD be omitted.

The attributes might not be returned in response to LSUB. Subscription lists are often not updated when the mailbox structure changes, so a client MUST NOT assume hierarchy information is kept there.

With the RLIST command from RFC 2193, a mailbox whose children are reachable only by referral shows \HasNoChildren in a LIST response and \HasChildren in an RLIST response.
sections.eli5: A folder cannot say both that it has folders inside and that it has none. Also, a folder that can never hold folders is a different thing from a folder that just has none right now.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
If a mailbox has children the current user cannot access, the server SHOULD respond with \HasNoChildren. A server that cannot cheaply check access may send \HasChildren anyway, which reveals more about the mailbox than intended.

A server built with that concern in mind SHOULD NOT attach \HasChildren unless it is certain the user can access at least one child.
sections.eli5: If a folder has a secret folder inside, saying it has a folder inside gives away a little. Careful servers only say so when you are allowed to see inside.

data.title: LIST with CHILDREN attributes
data.code:
C: A001 LIST "" *
S: * LIST (\HasNoChildren) "/" INBOX
S: * LIST (\HasChildren) "/" ITEM_1
S: * LIST (\HasNoChildren) "/" ITEM_1/ITEM_1A
S: * LIST (\HasChildren) "/" ITEM_2
S: A001 OK LIST Completed
